Inconspicuous

in-kun-SPIK-yoo-us -- Latin in- ('not') + conspicuous (con- 'together' + specere 'to look'). · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Inconspicuous is not easily noticed; blending in rather than standing out.

The undercover officer chose an inconspicuous gray sedan instead of anything that might draw attention.

Worked Example

Hoping nobody would notice she'd arrived twenty minutes late, she slipped into the back row and tried to stay inconspicuous for the rest of the assembly.

That effort to blend in and avoid drawing any attention at all is exactly what it means to be inconspicuous.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unnoticeable: hard to notice, though not necessarily on purpose

camouflaged: deliberately disguised to blend completely into the surroundings

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

prominent: very noticeable or standing out clearly

flashy: showy and deliberately attention-grabbing

Where it sits · how hard it is to spot — unnoticeable → inconspicuous → camouflaged

unnoticeable vs. inconspicuous: Unnoticeable is milder than inconspicuous: a tiny sidewalk crack is simply easy to miss, while something inconspicuous blends into its surroundings so thoroughly that attention slides right past.

camouflaged vs. inconspicuous: Camouflaged is stronger than inconspicuous: an inconspicuous moth simply avoids attention, but a camouflaged one matches the bark so completely that even a hunting bird flies past it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: not (Latin)

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: thoroughly (an intensive form of Latin com-, 'with')

Root — spic

Root — spic: to look, see (from Latin specere, 'to look at')

Suffix — -uous

Suffix — -uous: full of, tending to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: In- ('not') + con- ('thoroughly' — an intensifier) + spic ('to look, see' — from Latin specere) + -uous ('full of, tending to'): Latin conspicuus meant 'clearly visible, catching the eye.' Add the negating in- and something inconspicuous is, quite literally, not apt to be looked at — easily passed over by the eye.

Use the root in a new word: inspector

Use the root in a new word: inspector: The building inspector checked every wire and pipe before approving the new apartment complex.

Root Check

Word Choice

Inconspicuous usually describes something that simply doesn't draw the eye, whether by accident or on purpose -- it's a slightly more formal word than 'plain' or 'unnoticeable.'
